title: Central and Inscribed Angles Assessment
description: Show mastery of central angles, inscribed angles, and intercepted arcs.

questions.question: Which angle is a central angle?
options: An angle with its vertex at the center of the circle
An angle with its vertex on the circle
An angle with its vertex outside the circle
Any angle that intercepts a major arc
questions.explanation: A central angle has its vertex at the center of the circle.

questions.question: Central angle angle AOB intercepts arc AB. If m angle AOB = 132 degrees, what is m arc AB?
questions.explanation: A central angle and its intercepted arc have equal measures.

questions.question: Inscribed angle angle ACB intercepts arc AB. If m arc AB = 88 degrees, what is m angle ACB?
questions.explanation: An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc: 88 divided by 2 is 44.

questions.question: An inscribed angle measures 64 degrees. Enter the measure of its intercepted arc in degrees.
questions.explanation: The intercepted arc is twice the inscribed angle: 2 x 64 = 128.

questions.question: If a central angle and an inscribed angle intercept the same arc, then the central angle is twice the inscribed angle.
questions.explanation: The central angle equals the arc, while the inscribed angle is half the arc.

questions.question: A central angle and an inscribed angle intercept the same arc. The inscribed angle measures 35 degrees. What is the central angle?
questions.explanation: For the same intercepted arc, the central angle is twice the inscribed angle: 2 x 35 = 70.

questions.question: An inscribed angle that intercepts a semicircle measures 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: A semicircle measures 180 degrees, and half of 180 is 90.

questions.question: An inscribed angle measures 41 degrees. Which central angle intercepts the same arc?
questions.explanation: The central angle is twice the inscribed angle when both intercept the same arc: 2 x 41 = 82.

questions.question: A central angle intercepts an arc of 115 degrees. Enter the measure of the central angle in degrees.
questions.explanation: A central angle equals its intercepted arc.

questions.question: Which statement is always true?
options: An inscribed angle equals its intercepted arc.
A central angle is half its intercepted arc.
An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.
questions.explanation: The inscribed angle theorem says an inscribed angle is half the measure of its intercepted arc.

questions.question: A student says an inscribed angle that intercepts a 150-degree arc also measures 150 degrees. Correct the mistake.
questions.correctAnswer: The student used the central angle rule. An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc, so the angle measures 75 degrees.
questions.explanation: Only central angles equal their intercepted arcs. Inscribed angles are half their intercepted arcs.

questions.question: Explain why a central angle is twice an inscribed angle when both intercept the same arc.
questions.correctAnswer: The central angle equals the intercepted arc, but the inscribed angle equals half of that same arc. Therefore the central angle is twice the inscribed angle.
questions.explanation: Both relationships point back to the same arc measure: central angle = arc, and inscribed angle = half the arc.
